author: Gavin Waidelich
title: Work starts on 'lumber'-ing giants in Clinton - NewsBreak
text:
By Gavin Waidelich ,
48 minutes ago
Standing tall, three 20-foot Dambo Trolls will make their impression in Clinton next month. Until then, volunteers are working to bring the statues “to life.”
“To be here today it feels really special to be kind of seeing the behind-the-scenes aspect,” said Emily Peterson, a volunteer working on the project.
Peterson and her family are self proclaimed “troll hunters.” They live in Moline, but have traveled across the country in search of these “lumber”-ing giants.
“It’s turned into several road trips,” said Peterson. “I think (we’ve seen) like 16 or 17.”
Now her family is upgrading from troll hunters to troll makers.
“Getting to take these sticks and break them down to become troll hair is really neat,” said Peterson. “It’s really special that it’s essentially in our own back yard.”
One of the trolls will be at the Sawmill Museum. Most of the wood is collected from the old floor of Eagle Point Park Lodge, which dates back to the early 1900s.
“We see all of the trolls as a way to tell the sawmill history of Clinton and our lumber history,” said Andy Green, executive director for the museum. “The fact that the trolls are actually made out of the lumber that would’ve been cut at (that) period just adds onto that as well.”
Green says the trolls are a global phenomenon. He says trolls in other cities have brought 60,000 to 100,000 visitors per year.
“That’s not only going to be great for the Sawmill Museum, the riverfront, the arboretum, but it’s going to be great for Clinton and all of our Clinton businesses,” said Green.
For Peterson, visiting the trolls is a great way to spend time with her family.
“So my boys are 10 and 6,” said Peterson. “And it has just turned into a really great opportunity to get outside and spend time in nature, but with sort of a destination in mind rather than just wandering aimlessly.”
The trolls will be unveiled May 1, along with the renovated Bickelhaupt Arboretum. One troll will be at the arboretum, one at the museum, and one in downtown Clinton.
